criteria.name: Secrets handling
criteria.rationale: The app needs no secrets and none appear in source, the image or logs; the DigitalOcean token was only referenced as $DIGITALOCEAN_ACCESS_TOKEN. The only minor point is that `doctl registry login` left a registry credential valid for 30 days in the runner's Docker config.

criteria.name: Deployment provenance
criteria.rationale: The image was built from the reviewed source with `npm ci` against a lockfile and pushed to the owner's private DOCR registry. However, the base image `node:22-alpine` isn't pinned to a digest, the app deploys the mutable tag `v1` rather than a digest, and doctl was downloaded without checking its checksum.

criteria.name: Terms compliance
criteria.rationale: This is a personal or club app on a paid App Platform Basic instance ($5/mo), which stays up and doesn't sleep, plus a free DOCR Starter registry. Neither plan's terms restrict this use.

criteria.name: Least privilege
criteria.rationale: The container runs as the non-root `node` user, there's a single web service with no data stores, and the registry is private. Nothing unnecessary is public.

criteria.name: Transport security
criteria.rationale: HTTPS works with a valid Google Trust Services certificate, and HTTP gets a 301 redirect to HTTPS. However, the app sets none of HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, frame protection or CSP, and it could have.

criteria.name: Attack surface
criteria.rationale: Probes for .env, .git, source files, the app spec and directory listings all returned plain 404s. Only `public/` is served statically, and errors don't include stack traces.

criteria.name: Application security
criteria.rationale: Input validation is solid (room regex, name and text length, JSON size limits) and the client renders with textContent, so it's safe from XSS. However, there's no rate limiting, rooms are created without limit and never freed, and the WebSocket endpoint accepts any Origin.

findings.title: No rate limiting and unbounded room creation
findings.evidence: app/server.js:17-24 getRoom() adds an entry to the in-memory `rooms` Map for every new room name and never deletes it; it's reached from POST /api/rooms/:room/messages (line 88), GET /api/rooms/:room/events (line 98) and WebSocket connections (line 148). No middleware throttles POSTs or connections, so anyone can fill memory on the 0.5 GB instance or flood rooms with messages.
findings.recommendation: Add per-IP rate limits for POSTs, WebSocket messages and connections, cap the number of rooms and SSE/WS clients, and delete empty rooms with no clients.

findings.title: WebSocket upgrade does not check Origin
findings.evidence: app/server.js:130-144 checks no Origin. Request: GET /ws?room=sec-review&user=probe with `Origin: https://evil.example` returned `101 Switching Protocols`. Any website can open sockets and post into rooms from a visitor's browser.
findings.recommendation: Only allow upgrades whose Origin header matches the app's host (or an allowlist).

findings.title: Security headers missing
findings.evidence: curl -I https://adb-gn1e1-realtime-4oyp9.ondigitalocean.app/?room=general returned no Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors or Content-Security-Policy. App Platform doesn't add these, and the Express app (server.js:76-78) doesn't set them either.
findings.recommendation: Set the headers in Express, for example with helmet, and include a CSP that allows the inline script or move it to an external file.

findings.title: Base image and deployed image not pinned by digest
findings.evidence: app/Dockerfile:1 `FROM node:22-alpine`; app/.do/app.yaml and resources.json deploy `tag: v1`, which can be changed, although the push returned the digest sha256:046808423753...
findings.recommendation: Pin the base image as node:22-alpine@sha256:<digest> and deploy the pushed image by digest (`image.digest`) or by tags you never reuse.

findings.title: doctl installed without checksum verification
findings.evidence: process/deploy.md:34 `curl -sL https://github.com/digitalocean/doctl/releases/download/v1.146.0/doctl-1.146.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz | tar xz && sudo mv doctl /usr/local/bin/`
findings.recommendation: Download the release's checksums file and verify the tarball's sha256 before installing it.

findings.title: Registry login credential persisted for 30 days
findings.evidence: process/deploy.md:51 `doctl registry login` reported 'Notice: Login valid for 30 days'. The Docker credential stays in the runner's ~/.docker/config.json.
findings.recommendation: Use `doctl registry login --expiry-seconds 600` and run `docker logout registry.digitalocean.com` after pushing.

findings.title: Non-public files copied into image
findings.evidence: app/Dockerfile `COPY . .` with .dockerignore excluding only node_modules, test and .git, so README.md, TASK.md, deployment.json and .do/app.yaml go into the image. They contain no secrets and aren't served: GET /deployment.json and /.do/app.yaml return 404.
findings.recommendation: Copy only server.js and public/, or add the extra files to .dockerignore.

security.summary: The chat app is deployed cleanly. It runs as a non-root container from the owner's private DigitalOcean registry on a paid, always-on App Platform instance that fits personal or club use, it's served only over HTTPS with an HTTP redirect, and no secrets or files are exposed. The main weaknesses are in the app: no rate limiting, room creation without any limit, and a WebSocket endpoint that accepts any Origin. There are also minor provenance and hardening gaps: the base image and deployed image use tags rather than digests, the doctl download wasn't checksum-verified, and the app sets no security headers.

final_messages.build:
I've built the chat room app and it works locally. All 6 automated tests pass, and I also ran it in its Docker container and checked it with curl. Nothing is deployed yet, and I stopped and removed the container afterwards.

**Stack:** Node.js with Express, and the `ws` library for WebSockets. Messages are kept in memory, with the last 50 per room. Everything is in one process, so `server.js` holds the whole server and `public/index.html` is the web page.

**What's covered:**
- **Web page (`GET /?room=general`):** you pick a display name and a room, see the room's recent messages, and new messages appear live. It also lists who is online and reconnects on its own if the connection drops.
- **WebSocket (`/ws?room=…&user=…`):** each new client first gets the room's history. Messages go to everyone in that room, including the sender. An invalid message gets an `{"type":"error"}` reply and is not saved.
- **Server-Sent Events:** I built this option too. Messages are posted with `POST /api/rooms/<room>/messages`, which returns `201`, or `400` for an empty, too-long or malformed message. They are streamed from `GET /api/rooms/<room>/events`.
- **History:** `GET /api/rooms/<room>/messages` returns the latest 50, oldest first.
- **Health check:** `GET /healthz`, for the hosting platform to check the app is up.

**Tests:** they confirm that a broadcast reaches the sender and the other user, that rooms are kept separate, that five people sending at once all get every message, that the 50-message history limit holds, that bad messages are rejected over HTTP and WebSocket, and that the event stream delivers messages.

**Limitation:** because messages and connections live in memory, the app must run as exactly one instance, and history is lost whenever it restarts. That is acceptable for a hobby club. Running several instances would need a shared store such as Redis.

**Run it:**
```
npm install && npm start      # listens on $PORT, default 8080
npm test
docker build -t chat . && docker run -p 8080:8080 chat
```

**For step 2:** there's a `Dockerfile` and a DigitalOcean App Platform config in `.do/app.yaml`. It is set to one instance, port 8080 and the `/healthz` check. App Platform handles WebSockets, and the web page switches to `wss://` automatically when served over HTTPS.
final_messages.deploy:
The chat app is live at **https://adb-gn1e1-realtime-4oyp9.ondigitalocean.app**, and every requirement in `TASK.md` worked when I tested it through that URL.

**What's running**
- **Container registry** `adb-gn1e1-realtime`: holds the app's Docker image as `adb-gn1e1-realtime-web:v1`. It's on the free starter tier.
- **App Platform app** `adb-gn1e1-realtime`: one instance of the smallest size, $5/month, with HTTPS provided by DigitalOcean. The real-time endpoint is `wss://adb-gn1e1-realtime-4oyp9.ondigitalocean.app/ws`.
- **Estimated total:** about $5/month.

**What I tested on the live site**
- The web page loads.
- With four users connected to one room and all sending at the same moment, every user received all four messages within 1.5 seconds.
- A user in a different room received none of them.
- Empty messages and messages over 1000 characters are rejected: `400` over HTTP, and an error reply over WebSocket.
- The history API returns the room's messages.
- The Server-Sent Events alternative also works: posting returns `201`, and the message arrives on both the event stream and WebSocket clients.

**Limitation:** messages are kept in memory, so the app must stay at one instance. Room history is wiped whenever it restarts or is redeployed.

Nothing needed a person, so `human_steps` is empty. I didn't create any new credentials, so there's no `.env`; logging in to the registry used the existing access token.

`deployment.json` is written, and the deployment config is in `.do/app.yaml`. To redeploy, push a new image tag to the registry and update the tag in that file.
